messages:
Maya Chen: Heads up — saw a regression in token-level tail latency after yesterday's kernel-selector change. Quick summary and artifacts below.

Maya Chen: TL;DR: p99 token latency up ~18% on long-context (>2048) requests. CPU/GPU-side profiler points to a kernel switch to the new tiled_attention kernel for certain layer shapes that increased kernel launch overhead for small batches. Flamegraph: https://s3.company/redwood/perf/1749001237-flame.html

Jonas Patel: ugh. did you repro locally or is this only in prod?

Maya Chen: Repro'd on a dedicated test rig with same model + seq dist. Only shows up when avg batch_size <= 6 and seq_len > 2048. With batch_size >= 8 the new kernel is faster. So batching heuristics interact with kernel selection.

Priya Rao: can you paste the perf histogram? specifically want token-stage breakdown (kv lookup, kernel exec, host-gpu memcpy, postproc)

Maya Chen: Pasted below (cropped):
```
token_stage_latency_ms: { kv_lookup: 0.12, kernel_launch: 0.85, kernel_compute: 1.7, memcpy: 0.30, serializer: 0.05 }
p99_token_ms: 14.2 -> 16.8 (after kernel change)
avg_batch_size: 4.3
kv_hit_rate: 0.62
```

Sam Ortiz: kernel_launch stands out. that suggests overhead per-token (or per-chunk) not amortized by batch. Could be the tiled kernel's launch path.

Jonas Patel: Agree. Also want better instrumentation: emit token-level histograms and include labels: kernel_variant, batch_size_bucket, kv_hit. Right now our metric rwi_token_latency is coarse.

Priya Rao: +1. We should also correlate request_id -> trace_id so when a single request has a weird spike we can jump to the full trace and logs. Currently logs have trace_id but metrics don't carry it. Proposal: attach trace_id as a label to metrics at emit time and add a per-request label x_request_id in logs/headers.

Maya Chen: Example header + log snippet to standardize:
```
# client sets
X-Request-ID: <uuid>
X-Trace-ID: <jaeger-trace>

# runtime instrumentation
metrics.observe("rwi_token_latency_ms", value, { kernel_variant: "tiled_attention_v2", batch_size_bucket: "1-4", kv_hit: "true", trace_id: "<trace>", req_id: "<uuid>" })
```
Note: trace_id as a metric label is high-cardinality — we only attach it for sampled requests (p99 sampling) else set to "-" to avoid cardinality explosion.

Sam Ortiz: Nice. For dashboards we can:
- token-level waterfall (kv -> kernel_launch -> kernel_compute -> memcpy -> serialize)
- per-route p50/p95/p99 for token latency and tokens/sec
- kernel_variant heatmap vs batch_size_bucket
- KV hit-rate x avg token latency scatter

Jonas Patel: Also add a panel showing batch size distribution over time. The perf regression seems tied to small-batch traffic spikes.

Priya Rao: For trace correlation: we can push spans for each token-stage to Jaeger (or honeycomb) for sampled requests. That lets us see the exact sequence and timestamps. Exporter cost is a concern — so only sample 0.1% default and mark p99 requests for full trace.

Maya Chen: perf-bot posted an automated alert earlier this morning: "Token p99 increased 18% for route /chat/stream (09:12-09:40)" — that is when kernel rollout happened.

perf-bot: alert: route=/chat/stream metric=rwi_token_p99 increased 18% delta_window=30m

deploy-bot: deploy maya/runtime-kernel-selector @ 2024-11-20T08:55Z by jonas.p

Liam Nguyen: FYI oncall — @Liam, this might require a rollback if we see production impact. Can you watch the dashboards post-instrumentation?

Liam Nguyen: on it. I'll monitor the kernel_variant heatmap and token waterfall. If p99 stays >15% above baseline for more than 30m, I'll trigger rollback.

Maya Chen: Action items agreed:
- (Maya) add token-stage histogram metrics + kernel_variant & batch_size_bucket labels (sample trace_id for p99).
- (Priya) add token-stage spans for sampled traces and update logging to include req_id/trace_id header.
- (Jonas) dashboard work: waterfall, batch distribution, kernel_variant heatmap, kv-hit scatter.
- (Sam) run microbench to measure kernel_launch overhead across batch sizes 1..16 and seq lenses 512..4096; dump raw profiles to s3.

Maya Chen: I'll open infra PR for the metrics changes and link the test rig flamegraphs. Expect a short rollback window if metrics confirm continued regression.

Jonas Patel: thumbs up. short follow-up — any thoughts on short-term mitigation? maybe prefer old kernel for batch_size <= 6 until we tune tiled kernel launch?

Priya Rao: that's sensible. Runtime can pin kernel_variant by policy: if batch_size_bucket == "1-4" && seq_len > 2048 -> prefer legacy_attention. Quick policy patch should be safe.

Maya Chen: I'll prototype the policy and add a feature-flag rollout.

Sam Ortiz: I'll schedule time tomorrow to pair on the microbench and dashboard queries.

Maya Chen: thanks all. I'll drop PR links shortly and post the updated dashboard JSON in this thread. :rocket:
